column3: Close to the Hebrew; “Praise of David” is rendered “A Psalm of Praise, of David.”
Close to the Hebrew; “To his greatness there is no inquiry” is rendered “His greatness is unsearchable.”
Close to the Hebrew; “The matters of your wonders” is rendered “Your wonderful works.”
Close to the Hebrew; NASB supplies the subject “men.”
Close to the Hebrew; “They will pour forth” is rendered “They shall eagerly utter.”
Close to the Hebrew; “Compassionate” is rendered “merciful.”
The Hebrew has the third person (“his mighty deeds … his kingdom”); NASB uses the second person, “Your mighty acts … Your kingdom.”
Close to the Hebrew; NASB follows the Hebrew and has no added line (“The LORD is faithful in all his words …”), which is found in the Septuagint.
Close to the Hebrew; “Faithful” (hasid) is rendered “kind.”
Close to the Hebrew; “So it may bless” is rendered “will bless.”
